questions.question: The intelligence tests, according to R. C. Hutchinson, are designed to test:

questions.question: Our groves were planted to console at noon the ________ wanderer in their shades.
questions.explanation: In 'Ode on Solitude' / prescribed poetry, groves console the melancholic wanderer at noon.

questions.explanation: Alexander Pope's 'Ode on Solitude' opens with 'Happy the man whose wish and care, / A few paternal acres bound.'

questions.explanation: In 'Polythene Bag', hurt melts down with a touch of warmth.

questions.explanation: In 'Radha', her companions/friends at times banish her sadness.

questions.explanation: In Puran Singh's 'The Koel', the bird is restless for her beloved.

questions.question: The ________ is challenging the mountain.
questions.explanation: In 'The Porter', the mountain porter challenges the steep mountain.

questions.question: The children used to lean on their ________ to hear Martha's stories.
questions.explanation: In Walter de la Mare's 'Martha', the children leaned on their elbows to listen to her stories.

questions.question: Music in the villages, according to William Cowper, is provided by the ________.
questions.explanation: In 'God Made the Country', William Cowper notes birds provide natural music in the villages.

questions.question: The poet wants to live unseen and ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Ode on Solitude', the poet wishes to live 'unseen, unknown'.

questions.question: Durga Prasad Panda is primarily a ________.
questions.explanation: Durga Prasad Panda (poet of 'Polythene Bag') is a linguist and poet.

questions.explanation: In 'The Empty Heart', the greedy rich man sold his property to gather gold.

questions.question: Laxmi Prasad Devkota, a Nepali, obtained the B.A. degree from ________ University.
questions.explanation: Laxmi Prasad Devkota graduated from Patna University.

questions.explanation: In 'Martha', fairies and gnomes came out in the leaf-green light.

questions.question: Halku and Munni were always in ________.
questions.explanation: In Premchand's 'January Night' ('Poos Ki Raat'), Halku and Munni were always in debt.

questions.question: There are ________ general approaches to the treatment of allergic diseases.
questions.explanation: In 'Allergy', there are three general approaches to treating allergic diseases.

questions.question: Fifteen years before, the banker had too many ________ to count.
questions.explanation: In Anton Chekhov's 'The Bet', the banker had too many millions to count fifteen years earlier.

questions.question: The author knew Mr. Gessler from the days of his ________.
questions.explanation: In John Galsworthy's 'Quality', the narrator knew Mr. Gessler from the days of his extreme youth.

questions.question: Nurse said to Sun, "Now you're in your ________ costume."
questions.explanation: In 'Sun and Moon', the nurse puts Sun in a Russian costume.

questions.question: Looking at the mirror, the mother felt ________ all of a sudden.
questions.explanation: Looking into the mirror, the mother suddenly felt weary.

questions.question: The narrator could not marry his girlfriend because of opposition from his ________.
questions.explanation: In 'February / Love Defiled', parental opposition prevented the marriage.

questions.question: Halku took some ________ from the pit and filled his pipe.
questions.explanation: Halku took warm ash from the pit to fill his chillum/pipe.

questions.question: ________ provides temporary relief from allergies.
questions.explanation: Antihistamines offer temporary relief from allergic symptoms.

questions.explanation: In 'The Bet', the lawyer was kept under strictest observation in solitary confinement.

questions.question: Mr. Gessler died of ________.
questions.explanation: In 'Quality', the dedicated bootmaker Mr. Gessler died of slow starvation.

questions.question: Sun was dressed in ________.
questions.explanation: Sun was dressed in a white shirt/outfit.

questions.question: Binapani Mohanty won the Sahitya Akademi Award for ________.
questions.explanation: Binapani Mohanty received the Sahitya Akademi Award for 'Pata Dei'.

questions.question: The girl wore a ________ when she came to meet the narrator the last time.
questions.explanation: On their last meeting, she wore a yellow dress.

questions.question: The old civilization and culture have grown and changed only in ________.
questions.explanation: Only India has preserved and continually adapted its ancient civilization and culture.

questions.question: "Old woman, I hold in my hand a bird" is from:
questions.explanation: This line is from Toni Morrison's 'Once Upon a Time'.

questions.question: The ________ felt that they had travelled back into the past when the incidents of Martha's stories had taken place.
questions.explanation: The listeners felt transported back to the time of Martha's stories.

questions.question: Which work of Premchand was banned by the British Government?
questions.explanation: Premchand's early collection of patriotic stories 'Soz-e-Watan' ('Soje Vatan') was banned by the British authorities.

questions.question: The poem "The Empty Heart" tells us about ________.
questions.explanation: 'The Empty Heart' warns against insatiable greed.

questions.question: What keeps coming back again and again in 'Polythene Bag'?

questions.explanation: Satyajit Ray was awarded an honorary doctorate by the University of Oxford.

questions.explanation: In 'The Empty Heart', his prayer was granted sevenfold.

questions.question: Active voice of "A mistake has been committed by him" is:
options: A mistake was committed by him.
A mistake had committed by him.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive ('has been committed') converts to present perfect active ('He has committed a mistake.').

questions.question: Active voice of "The prices were lowered by the shopkeeper" is:
options: The shopkeeper got down the prices.
questions.explanation: Simple past passive ('were lowered by the shopkeeper') converts to simple past active ('The shopkeeper lowered the prices.').

questions.question: Active voice of "We are taught grammar by him" is:
options: Grammar was taught to us by him.
We were teached grammar by him.
questions.explanation: Present simple passive ('are taught') converts to present simple active ('He teaches us grammar.').

questions.question: Passive voice of "We must respect the elders" is:
options: The elders must respected by us.
The elders are respected by we.
The elders deserve respect from us.
questions.explanation: Modal passive uses 'must be + V3' ('The elders must be respected.').

questions.question: Passive voice of "We have warned you" is:
questions.explanation: Present perfect active ('have warned') becomes passive 'have been warned'.

questions.question: Passive voice of "The boy laughed at the beggar" is:
options: The beggar was laughed by the boy.
The beggar was being laughed by the boy.
The beggar was being laughed at by the boy.
The beggar was laughed at by the boy.
questions.explanation: Prepositional verb 'laughed at' retains 'at' in passive voice: 'The beggar was laughed at by the boy.'

questions.question: Direct speech of "I asked him why he was working so hard" is:
options: I said to him, "Why are you working so hard?"
I asked with him, "Why you working so hard?"
I told him, "Why do you work so hard?"
I asked to him, "Why have you to work so hard?"
questions.explanation: 'Why he was working' shifts back to present continuous question '"Why are you working so hard?"'

questions.question: Direct speech of "The doctor advised the patient to take complete rest" is:
options: The doctor asked the patient, "Take rest."
The doctor said to the patient, "Take complete rest."
The doctor suggested to the patient, "You should take complete rest."
The doctor asks the patient, "Take complete rest."
questions.explanation: Imperative advice 'to take complete rest' corresponds to '"Take complete rest."'

questions.question: Direct speech of "She said that they could leave the books there" is:
options: She says, "You can leave the books there."
She said, "You can leave the books here."
She asks, "You must leave the books there."
She ordered, "You can leave the books there."
questions.explanation: 'Could' shifts back to 'can' and 'there' shifts back to 'here' in direct speech.

questions.question: Direct speech of "The police ordered the thief not to move" is:
options: The police said to the thief, "Don't move."
The police ordered the thief, "Not move."
The police told to the thief, "Don't move."
The police asked the thief, "Don't move."
questions.explanation: Negative imperative 'not to move' corresponds to '"Don't move."'

questions.question: Indirect speech of: He said, "Alas! I am ruined." is:
options: He said that he was ruined.
He exclaimed sadly that he was ruined.
He cried that he has been ruined.
He shouted that he is ruined.
questions.explanation: 'Alas!' expresses sorrow, so 'exclaimed sadly' is appropriate and 'am ruined' shifts to 'was ruined'.

questions.question: Indirect speech of: Everybody said, "How well she sings!" is:
options: Everybody told us that she sings very well.
Everybody exclaimed with admiration that she sings very well.
Everybody exclaimed that she sang very well.
Everybody told us that how she sang very well.
questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentence in past tense shifts 'sings' to past tense 'sang very well'.

questions.question: I will never ________ her.
questions.explanation: After modal 'will', the base verb 'forget' is used.

questions.question: I ________ him very well.
questions.explanation: First-person singular 'I' takes the base verb 'know'.

questions.question: When do you ________ milk?
questions.explanation: After auxiliary 'do', the base verb 'take' is used.

questions.question: Reeta ________ me this dress.
questions.explanation: Simple past 'gave' is grammatically complete with subject 'Reeta'.

questions.question: They were ________ fishes.
questions.explanation: 'Were + V-ing' ('catching') forms the past continuous tense.

questions.question: What ________ he doing at this moment?
questions.explanation: 'At this moment' with singular 'he' requires 'is'.

questions.question: It ________ to rain.
questions.explanation: 'It is going to rain.' is the natural predictive expression.

questions.question: Don't depend ________ others.
questions.explanation: 'Depend on' is the standard preposition.

questions.question: Dr. Singh concluded the speech ________ explaining the importance of charity.
questions.explanation: 'Concluded ... by + gerund' indicates the manner/means of ending the speech.

questions.question: A thorough search was carried ________ in the whole building.
questions.explanation: 'Carry out' means to conduct or execute a search/task.

questions.question: Don't put ________ until tomorrow what you can do today.
questions.explanation: 'Put off' means to postpone or delay.

questions.question: I can cope ________ any problem.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'cope with'.

questions.question: The criminal was totally taken ________ when the police recognised him.
questions.explanation: 'Taken aback' means shocked or surprised.

questions.question: We warned her ________ the danger.
questions.explanation: 'Warn someone of danger' is the standard preposition usage.

questions.question: Translate into English: मैं अगले साल अमेरिका जा रही हूँ।
options: I go to America next year.
I am going to America next year.

questions.explanation: 'Fast' already functions as an adverb ('fastly' is non-standard), and singular 'She' takes 'speaks'.

questions.question: Synonym of 'Defect' is:
questions.explanation: 'Shortcoming' is a synonym of 'defect'.

questions.question: Synonym of 'Imitate' is:
questions.explanation: 'Copy' means to imitate.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
We sometimes think it would be very nice to have no work to do. Now we envy rich people who have not to work for their living, but can do just what pleases them all the year round. Yet when we feel like this, we make a mistake. Sometimes rich people are not as happy as we think, because they are tired of having nothing to do. Most of us are happy when we have regular work to do for our living especially if the work is what we like to do.
Questions: (i) What do we think sometimes? (ii) Why do we envy rich people? (iii) Why are rich people not as happy as we think they are? (iv) What makes us happy?
OR Passage on Science and machinery.
questions.explanation: Subjective comprehension question (7 marks).

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
Some people think that the aim of education is merely to give knowledge. These people want students to read books, and do nothing else but add to their knowledge. Others believe that knowledge alone is not enough; only that which enables a man to earn his living can be called education. Some people think that knowledge is more important, others believe that education should solely aim at making good citizens. In fact, education should aim at giving knowledge as well as self-reliance.
Questions: (i) What do some people think to be the aim of education? (ii) What do others think? (iii) What is the true aim of education? (iv) Why do some people want students to only read books?
OR Passage on Australia.
questions.explanation: Subjective comprehension question (7 marks).

questions.question:
Read the poem carefully and answer:
'The Leader' (Patient and steady with all he must bear...) OR 'I live in a town, in a street...'
Questions: (i) Why should a leader be patient and steady? (ii) What does the poet mean by 'solid as steel'? (iii) Why is a leader called bold?
questions.explanation: Subjective poetry comprehension question (6 marks).

questions.question:
Answer any five of the following questions:

(b) What does the cinema combine?
(c) How did the Pre-Aryans build up a new civilization?
(d) What does Aris say about the fight going on in Rangoon?
(e) Who is a blessed man?
(f) Why was the tree called unkind?
(g) How did Martha tell her stories?
(h) What fires the koel?
(i) How did the daughter shoulder her responsibilities?
(j) What was Mr. Gessler's complaint against big firms?
